_source: design/08 §1.2's table, enforced by tools/size-budget.mjs (the artifact lines) and tools/treeshake-check.mjs (the min+gz lines). Every number is BYTES, because a budget expressed in 'KB' is a budget nobody can diff; 1 KB = 1024 B, the unit §1.2 uses. Changing any line here is a reviewed act with the reason in the commit message and, where the new value is looser than design's, an entry in `_overDesign` — which `size-budget.mjs` and `treeshake-check.mjs` both enforce mechanically (the same rule bench/runtime/budget.json applies to the perf gates, R9).

_design._why: design/08 §1.2's own column, printed beside the measurement on every run so drift from the design document is visible even inside budget.

design/08 §1.2 budgets the kit at ≤ 8 MB unpacked (hard fail 12 MB) and its single bundle file at ≤ 2 MB. There is no bundle line here because there is no bundle: §3.1 bundles the kit with esbuild because CLI cold-start matters, and the CLI does not exist yet (no `bin`, no `src/cli.ts`). The kit ships unbundled `tsc` output with `pg` as a real runtime dependency, so the 2 MB bundle line is not applicable rather than passing — see the AS BUILT note under design/08 §3.1.

treeshake._why: design/08 §1.2's min+gz lines, measured by §2.4's method: gzip(esbuild --bundle --format=esm --minify --platform=node) of fixtures/treeshake/<case>/entry.ts resolved THROUGH the package's export map, with rollup + @rollup/plugin-node-resolve run beside it as the independent DCE second opinion. §1.2 says these are provisional and get baselined on the first measurement, then ratcheted downward only.
treeshake._baselined: provisional, baselined 2026-08-28; re-baselined 2026-08-28 for design/11 §3 K2a (the DSL gained .references/.check/.unique(name,opts)/.comment/.renamedFrom, the check/foreignKey/unique/renamedFrom extras, pgSchema and src/schema/ddl.ts). Every number below moved UP by the same rule the first baseline used — budget = min(design, ceil(measured / 1024) * 1024) — and two of the three remain below design/08 §1.2. The module-set goldens gained exactly one entry, dist/schema/ddl.js, which is what design §2.4 step 3 wants a reviewer to see.
treeshake._rule: budget = min(design, ceil(measured / 1024) * 1024). Rounding the measurement up to the next whole KB and never above design's number ratchets three of the four cases BELOW design on their first measurement, and leaves ~2% of headroom so that a comment edit in packages/pg-prime/src does not turn the package job red. The zero-tolerance regression detector for these fixtures is not the byte count — it is fixtures/treeshake/<case>/expected-modules.json, the exact set of modules that contributed bytes, which is what design §2.4 step 3 says actually works.

_measured._when: 2026-08-28 (design/11 §3 K2a), esbuild 0.28.2, node 24.14.1, packages/pg-prime built with typescript 7.0.2

_measuredBeforeK2a._when: 2026-08-28, the packaging pass (a5f4f9a). Kept so the K2a delta reads as +921 / +911 / +1656 B min+gz rather than as an absolute.

_overDesign._why: Every entry is a budget deliberately looser than design/08 §1.2's number, with the reason and the measurement. `size-budget.mjs` FAILS on a budget that exceeds its `_design` twin and is not listed here, so widening one is a machine-checkable event and not only a review one. An entry leaves this block by measurement — by the number coming down — never by editing the number.
_overDesign.treeshake.connect-one-select: design/08 §1.2 budgets 'connect + one select' at 35 KB min+gz; it measures 47 212 B (46.1 KB), 32% over, and the budget is baselined at 48 128 B and ratchets down from there. (46 291 B before design/11 §3 K2a added the DDL-affecting modifiers, the four new extras, `pgSchema` and `src/schema/ddl.ts` to the schema layer: +921 B, and `dist/schema/ddl.js` is the one module the goldens gained.) The reason is structural and worth writing down rather than shaving: the query builder is ONE object graph. `compileOnly(schema)` / `pgPrime({driver, schema})` both go through `makeExecutor`, and the executor object carries `from` / `insertInto` / `update` / `deleteFrom` / `with` as methods, so the insert, update, delete and CTE builders are reachable from the first line of any program that opens a handle — `query/insert.js` alone is 9 121 B of the bundle. Add the emitter (`compile/compiler.js` 16 268 B + `compile/hoist.js` 13 890 B), which every compile needs, the builtin codec table (`codec/builtins.js` 15 854 B), which the default registry needs, and `driver/pg-adapter.js` (12 202 B), which `pgDriver(pool)` is, and 46 KB is what one select costs. The honest headline is the OTHER number in this file: the ENTIRE package, every export referenced, is 50 004 B min+gz against design's 122 880 ceiling — so the package is 2.4x smaller than design budgeted and the tree-shaking GRANULARITY inside the query builder is coarse, with 93% of the whole library reachable from `connect + one select`. The two goldens prove it rather than assert it: fixtures/treeshake/connect-one-select and fixtures/treeshake/full-crud-tx include the IDENTICAL 39 package modules — adding insert, update, delete and `db.transaction()` to a program that already opens a handle and runs one select adds no module at all, and 369 bytes of gzip. Making this line meet 35 KB is a code change (splitting the executor's method surface so unused builders are not reachable from the handle), not a budget change, and it is not in the packaging pass's scope. Recorded in design/08 §2.4 AS BUILT.
_overDesign.packages/pg-prime.largestDtsBytes: design/08 §1.2's canary is 40 KB per declaration file and `dist/query/types.d.ts` measures 54 843 B (53.6 KB) — 34% over. The file is design/03's type layer: `Db`, `Query`, the ~40 operand and projection types, the join/group/set-op state machine. Splitting it is a PUBLIC-API refactor (every one of those names is re-exported from the root barrel and pinned by tools/api-snapshot/pg-prime.json), which is out of scope for the packaging pass that added this gate. bench/types/run.mjs has been measuring the same file at 54 808 B under TypeScript 5.9.3 since WS7, so this is a known, stable number rather than a new regression. The budget is therefore RATCHET-ONLY: it is set AT the measurement, so any growth at all fails CI and needs a visible diff to this file. Design's 40 960 stays in `_design` and is printed beside the measurement on every run.
